back: Short-term unemployment of people between jobs or searching for their first job.
Long-term unemployment caused by a change in the structure of the economy, leaving a mismatch of skills or location.
Unemployment caused by a fall in aggregate demand in a downturn (also called demand-deficient unemployment).
Unemployment at certain times of the year because demand for some workers depends on the season.
Structural unemployment concentrated in one area, often after its main industry declines.
Unemployment caused when machines or new methods replace workers; a form of structural unemployment.

front: How can you tell cyclical unemployment in data?
back: It rises in many industries and regions at the same time as output falls.
Frictional: job information. Structural: retraining, mobility. Cyclical: raise aggregate demand. Seasonal: off-season work, irrigation.
